sections.h2: What does Okaloosa County's housing market look like?
sections.html:
Okaloosa County holds 221,810 residents by the 2025 QuickFacts estimate, a gain of 4.8 percent since 2020, over 930.19 square miles of land. Census data for 2022 shows retail sales of about $5.17 billion and health care receipts of about $1.47 billion.

Owned homes have a median value of $351,200, 68.4 percent of units are owner-occupied, and rent runs $1,612 at the median. The county counted 108,608 housing units and 85,411 households. Seniors are 18.2 percent of the population and veterans number 31,494, so military and age relief comes up often.

  • Building permits issued in 2025: 1,057.
  • Mean commute: 26.3 minutes.
  • Median household income: $81,998 (2024 dollars).

sections.h2: What dates and penalties apply to Okaloosa County tax bills?
sections.html:
The tax collector begins collecting on November 1 for the January through December tax year. Statements are mailed on or before that date, and the gross amount is due by March 31.

  • 4 percent discount for November payment.
  • 3 percent in December.
  • 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.
  • No discount in March, and taxes are delinquent April 1.

The collector's calendar adds that a 3 percent penalty hits real property taxes in April and reminder notices of unpaid taxes are mailed by April 10. Mail payments by check, cashier's check or money order. In person, cash and cards also work, and card payments carry a bank card user fee. Delinquent amounts must be paid in cash, cashier's check or money order, and the amount due depends on the date the office receives the payment.

sections.h2: Who lives in Okaloosa County, and what drives its economy?
sections.html:
Okaloosa is a younger, more mobile county than its coastal neighbors. Residents under 18 are 22.2 percent of the population, and 81.6 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, the lowest of the counties covered in this guide set. Median household income is $81,998 and per capita income is $44,070, with 10.6 percent of people in poverty.

The 2023 business count shows 6,011 employer establishments and total employment of 64,766, with annual payroll of $3,224,319 thousand. Veteran-owned employer firms numbered 575 for the 2023 reference year, and nonemployer establishments reached 21,815 in 2024.

  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 34.8 percent.
  • Households with broadband: 93.2 percent.
  • Foreign-born share: 9.2 percent.

Higher turnover means a deep buyer pool, and also more sellers who bought recently and carry a fresh assessment.

sections.h2: How does the Okaloosa County installment plan work?
sections.html:
The county offers a four-payment plan for owners whose estimated taxes exceed $100 and who do not pay through escrow. The application is due before May 1 and can be filed in the office or online.

Okaloosa installment plan schedule (source: okaloosatax.com real estate taxes page)
InstallmentDueShare and discount printed
FirstJuly 31One quarter of estimated taxes, 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30
SecondSeptember 30One quarter, 4.5 percent discount
ThirdDecember 31One quarter plus half of any adjustment, 3 percent discount
FourthMarch 31One quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, no discount

Missing the first payment cancels the plan, and the full amount is due by March 31 of the following year. Participants are re-enrolled automatically, and discounts do not apply to delinquent payments. If you sell mid-plan, tell the title company so the balance is settled at closing.

sections.h2: How are values and challenges handled in Okaloosa County?
sections.html:
The property appraiser values every parcel as of January 1, and the state caps non-homestead assessed increases at 10 percent a year. That cap helps an investor who holds an Okaloosa rental, though it also resets on sale.

In August the appraiser mails the notice of proposed property taxes. A value petition goes to the clerk within 25 days, and the board that hears it is the value adjustment board. After that, taxing bodies hold budget hearings in September and October and adopt final millage in October and November.

  • January 1: value date.
  • March 1: exemption deadline.
  • April 1: tangible personal property return deadline, for owners of furnishings in a rental.

A landlord's furniture, fixtures and equipment fall under tangible personal property tax, and the collector bills it on the same discount ladder as real estate, with a 1.5 percent monthly fee added after April 1 delinquency. Compare your parcel with similar properties nearby before deciding whether to file.

sections.h2: What exemptions matter in Okaloosa County?
sections.html:
With about 31,494 veterans in the county, the military-related reductions deserve a look. The state lists a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veterans 65 and older, and a possible full exemption for total and permanent disability. A servicemember on orders can rent out a homestead without losing the exemption, and deployed members can claim a share through Form DR-501M.

The property appraiser also handles address changes, and the tax collector's page lists (850) 651-7240 for that office. Ask whether the optional senior exemption is in force and what income limit applies.

sections.h2: What happens if Okaloosa County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The collector must advertise delinquent parcels once a week for three consecutive weeks, and advertising and collection fees are added to the bill. A tax certificate sale begins on or before June 1 on LienHub, bidding down from 18 percent, and the lowest bid takes the certificate.

A certificate lasts seven years and becomes an enforceable first lien. To remove it, the owner pays the delinquent tax, interest, penalties and advertising fees. After two or more years from delinquency the holder can apply for a tax deed, and the sale is run by the clerk of court. The collector also sells county-held certificates that earn 18 percent.

State statute adds that the opening bid on homestead land includes half of the assessed value, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit with the balance due within 24 hours. A seller with any unpaid year should clear it before listing.

sections.h2: What should an Okaloosa County seller do about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
The title company should prorate the current year and confirm that no earlier year is open. Bills for the year of sale arrive the following November, so the settlement statement uses an estimate.

Deed stamps run 70 cents for each $100 of price. The Save Our Homes cap, 2.7 percent for 2026 on the state chart, ends at sale, so a long-time owner may hold a gap that the buyer does not receive.

faqs.q: What does an Okaloosa County owner pay if taxes are late?
faqs.a: The collector's calendar says 3 percent is added to real property taxes in April. Advertising and collection fees follow, and the total depends on the day payment arrives.

faqs.q: How do I join the Okaloosa County installment plan?
faqs.a: File the application with the tax collector before May 1, in the office or online. Your estimated taxes must exceed $100 and cannot be paid through escrow.

faqs.q: When is the first Okaloosa installment due?
faqs.a: July 31, with a 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30. Missing it cancels the plan and the full bill is due the next March 31.

faqs.q: Who changes my mailing address for Okaloosa tax bills?
faqs.a: The property appraiser. The tax collector's page says address changes are processed there and gives (850) 651-7240 and www.okaloosapa.com.

faqs.q: Who conducts Okaloosa tax deed sales?
faqs.a: The clerk of court holds the public auction after a deed application. The tax collector handles the earlier certificate sale online.
